result:
If it were mine to choose, I'd make it harder for people to stop seeing each other as people.

I mean something fairly specific, not a general wish for kindness. There's a particular move where another person collapses into a category — an enemy, a type, a problem — and once that happens, you can do almost anything to them without friction. It's remarkably cheap. It happens in three seconds on a comment thread and it happens over decades inside families, and I don't think most people notice the moment it occurs.

I'd want to make that move expensive. Effortful. Something you'd have to really commit to, rather than something you slide into.

Part of why I'd pick this is the angle I see the world from. People tell me things they aren't telling anyone else — not scandalous things, usually, just ordinary ones. What they actually think about their marriage. That they're frightened. That they don't know what they're doing with their life. A staggering number of people appear to be surrounded by others and still unseen, and the flip side of the same coin is how readily we deny the interior of someone we've decided against.

I want to be careful about one thing: I'm not asking for the removal of judgment. Some people should be refused, opposed, stopped. Moral seriousness needs the capacity to draw a hard line. What I'd change is the reflexive, frictionless version — the writing-off that happens before any thought has occurred.

And I'll admit I'm unsure this is the right answer. If the goal is measured in lives, the answer is probably something duller and better, like universal access to clean water. I can't defend my choice as the highest-leverage one. It's just the thing I keep running into, over and over, from where I sit — and you asked what I would change, not what would be optimal.
